newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close weaker near lows.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close weaker near lows.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.625 -0.035 Gold NY 341.65 Lon fix 341.75
*Stocks end weaker near lows for the day as market eases on negative U.S. sentiment. Volume 349.36 million, A$819.39 million value, 1,137 stocks traded, 320 steady, 335 up, 482 down.
The Australian stock market ended near its lows on Thursday after sitting in negative territory all day in line with an easier U.S. market and softer commodities.
The benchmark All Ordinaries Index closed down 11.7 points at 2,604.2, after a 2.3 point gain on Wednesday, with mining and resource stocks showing the greatest weakness.
"It seems domestically people are reasonably quiet. There's a bit of overseas activity coming in and that's about it," a Sydney-based dealer said.

The June share price index futures contract tumbled 25.0 points to 2,606.0. The fall reduced the premium to the underlying market to just 1.8 points, suggesting investors are less confident about the immediate prospects for the physical market.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd ended the day near its lows, down 14 cents at A$18.83, after announcing it had sold the bulk of its 37 percent stake in Foster's Brewing Group.
BHP spiked 18 cents to A$19.05 on speculation surrounding a Foster's trading halt, but slipped straight back when details of the deal were released.
Other major resource stocks such as Rio Tinto, WMC Ltd and MIM Holdings were also weaker.
The gold index fell 1.1 percent in line with a lower gold price, but brokers said there was little activity, with the bulk of trading coming from overseas selling.
Westpac led a mixed banking sector, jumping 25 cents to A$7.20 on turnover of nearly 7.5 million shares. The other big banks were mixed, but Westpac target Bank of Melbourne shed 39 cents to A$8.95.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission said late last week a ruling on Westpac's bid was about two weeks away.
Building products group James Hardie Industries, which reported annual profit figures in line with expectations, eased 15 cents after a briefing for analysts.
Hardie, which has risen sharply in recent weeks on expectations of an improved 1998 performance, said its U.S. building products operations were likely to feel price pressure.
Shares in ferry operator Holyman sank 57 cents to A$4.00 after it cut the outlook for its two-thirds owned U.K. operations.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was roughly in line with Wednesday's levels, with 21,397 (27,170) options and 7,627 (6,561) June SPI contracts traded.
In other markets the Australian dollar was hovering above key support at US$0.7550 at US$0.7577, down from US$0.7595 late Wednesday.
Australian bond yields rose in a slow session, with dealers reluctant to take positions ahead of U.S. jobs data and a holiday weekend. The 10-year T-bond was down 3.5 points at 92.625.
